MRI of right Knee with 
-Locator, SG PD FatSat, SG T2W FS, SG T1W, CO T2W FS, AX T2W FS, AX T2W

> Linear signal intensity in posterior horn of medial meniscus, with extending into the surface, in favor of tear.
> No strong MR evidence of tear of lateral meniscus.
> The contour of ACL, PCL and MCL appears to be within normal, no abnormal signal intensity is noted.
    Mild interstitial increased signal intensity of proxim LCL on F/S T2WI, in favor of degeneration.
> Wearing of articular cartilage and osteophyte of right knee and bone marrow edema in medial femoral condyle (major at subchondral region), reflecting osteoarthritis. 
> Joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis with suprapatellar and medial plicae; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis.
> A lobulated cystic lesion with internal septums in medial popliteal fossa between the tendons of the medial head of the gastrocnemius and the semimembranosus muscles, in favor of Baker's cyst, about 7 cm; in favor of hypertrophy synovium or tiny loose bodies in lower portion of the cyst and perifocal edema.

Impression: 
1. Osteoarthritis of right knee joint.
2. Synovitis of right knee with large Baker's cyst and perifocal edema.
3. Tear of posterior horn of medial meniscus.
4. R/O degeneration of LCL.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation

There is proximal non avulsive disruption of the anterior cruciate ligament, with some anteriorly displaced fragments being best appreciated in the sagittal plane.  
Marrow contusional changes are noted at the central portion of the lateral femoral condyle, also affecting the posteromedial and posterolateral tibial plateaux - the overall pattern being compatible with a pivot shift mechanism of injury.  
There is a significant resultant suprapatellar effusion with associated synovitis.  There are no convincing medial or lateral meniscal tears. A grade 1 proximal MCL injury is noted. There is furthermore a posteromedial meniscocapsular sprain. 
No posterolateral corner injury is identified, nor is there any injury to the anterolateral ligament. 
Normal PCL, lateral collateral ligament, popliteus musculotendinous unit and PTFL, distal iliotibial band and extensor tendons. Well-preserved tricompartmental hyaline articular cartilage surfaces.  
The extent of fluid signal intensity within the deep posterior soft tissues following injury suggests prior posterior capsular disruption.

Small suprapatellar knee joint effusion. No Baker's cyst.

Marrow signal is normal.

Moderate chondromalacia of the medial patella facet.

Complex oblique undersurface tear of the medial meniscus posterior horn.

Medial collateral ligament and supporting knee ligamentous structures are intact.
